title: When Galaxies Collide
objective: After this level you can explain galaxy collisions and the future merger of the Milky Way and Andromeda.
summary: Galaxies merge over hundreds of millions of years. Andromeda is heading our way, but stars almost never hit each other.

cards.headline: Andromeda is heading toward the Milky Way.
cards.body: Our biggest neighbor is on the move, and it's coming our way. Should you worry? Short answer: no. Long answer: a galaxy collision is stranger, and gentler, than it sounds.

cards.headline: The forecast
cards.body: Galaxies can collide and merge, pulling each other into new shapes over hundreds of millions of years. Andromeda, about 2.5 million light-years away, is moving toward the Milky Way. For years the forecast was a merger in about 4.5 billion years. Then a 2025 study put the chance of one within the next 10 billion years at only about 50%. The sure thing became a coin flip.
cards.callout: Merger: a coin flip within 10 billion years

cards.headline: Crash without a crash
cards.body: Even if it happens, don't picture a pileup. When galaxies collide, individual stars almost never hit each other, because the space between stars is so vast. The two galaxies pass through each other while their gravity reshapes both. Even a full merger leaves almost every star without a scratch.

cards.fact: You can see our galactic neighbor with your own eyes.
cards.context: From a dark site, Andromeda shows up to the naked eye as a faint smudge. That smudge is the galaxy in this story, about 2.5 million light-years away and heading our way. It's the rare forecast you can check from your backyard.
